style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A psalm for a bad generation -- the godly man has run out, the faithful have vanished, and everyone talks empty talk to his neighbor with smooth lips and 'a heart and a heart.' The tongues even have a manifesto: by our tongue we will win, our lips belong to us, who is lord over us? Into that noise one voice speaks -- the only time God speaks in the psalm -- 'Because the afflicted are plundered, because the needy groan, now I will arise,' and the arrogant go quiet. Then the psalm's famous verse sets the LORD's words against theirs: pure words, silver refined in a crucible, purified seven times -- no slag, no double heart. You will keep them, O LORD, from this generation forever. The last line refuses to pretend the generation has changed: the wicked still strut on every side when cheapness is exalted among men. But the psalm has already told you whose words hold.

1.text: For the choir director, on the Sheminith. A psalm of David. Save, O LORD, for the godly man is gone; the faithful have vanished from among the children of men.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Sheminith, A Psalm [mizmor] of David. Help ['Save', yasha, the KJV margin], LORD [YHWH]; for the godly man [chasid] ceases [gamar -- is finished]; for the faithful [aman -- the trustworthy] fail from among the children [ben] of men [adam].
1.notes: hoshiah YHWH ki-gamar chasid (H3467, H3068, H1584, H2623): 'Save!' -- the margin's word, the hoshiah of Hosanna -- because the chasid, the covenant-loyal man, has run out; ki-phassu emunim mi-bene adam (H539, H1121, H120): the faithful have vanished from humanity. Sheminith (H8067), 'the eighth', is a musical direction (also Psalm 6), perhaps a low register. The psalm's emergency is a shortage of honest people.

2.text: Everyone speaks empty words to his neighbor; with flattering lips and a double heart they talk.
2.amp: They speak [dabar] vanity [shav -- emptiness, falsehood] every one [ish] with his neighbour [rea]: with flattering [chelqah -- smooth] lips [saphah] and with a double ['an heart and an heart', leb, the KJV margin] heart do they speak [dabar].
2.notes: shav yedabberu ish et-reehu (H7723, H1696, H376, H7453): shav, emptiness -- the third commandment's word for what must not be attached to God's name -- is now the whole content of neighborly talk. sephat chalaqot be-leb va-leb yedabberu (H8193, H2513, H3820): smooth lips and 'a heart and a heart', the margin's literal for duplicity. One face for the neighbor, another kept back.

3.text: May the LORD cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaks big things --
3.amp: The LORD [YHWH] shall cut off [karath] all flattering [chelqah -- smooth] lips [saphah], and the tongue [lashon] that speaks [dabar] proud ['great', gadol, the KJV margin] things:
3.notes: yakhret YHWH kol-siphte chalaqot (H3772, H3068, H8193, H2513): the LORD will CUT OFF -- karath, the covenant-cutting verb turned to amputation -- all smooth lips. lashon medabberet gedolot (H3956, H1696, H1419): the tongue that talks 'great things', the margin's literal -- the boast of Daniel 7:8's little horn and James 3:5's small member.

4.text: those who say, 'By our tongue we will win; our lips belong to us -- who is lord over us?'
4.amp: Who have said [amar], With our tongue [lashon] will we prevail [gabar]; our lips ['are with us', saphah, the KJV margin] are our own: who is lord [adon] over us?
4.notes: asher ameru li-leshonenu nagbir (H559, H3956, H1396): 'by our tongue we will be strong' -- speech as a weapon of conquest; sephatenu ittanu mi adon lanu (H8193, H113): 'our lips are with us', the margin's literal -- ours, under no license -- 'who is lord over us?' The manifesto of autonomous speech, and the psalm's answer is verse 5: Someone is.

5.text: 'Because the afflicted are plundered, because the needy groan, now I will arise,' says the LORD; 'I will place him in safety from the one who snorts at him.'
5.amp: For the oppression [shod -- plundering] of the poor [ani -- afflicted], for the sighing [anaqah -- groaning] of the needy [ebyon], now will I arise [qum], says [amar] the LORD [YHWH]; I will set [shith] him in safety [yesha] from him that puffs ['would ensnare him', puach, the KJV margin] at him.
5.notes: mi-shod aniyyim me-anqat ebyonim (H7701, H6041, H603, H34): because of the plundering of the afflicted and the groaning of the needy -- attah aqum yomar YHWH (H6965, H559, H3068): NOW I will arise, says the LORD -- the only place in the psalm God speaks, and the tongues go quiet. ashit be-yesha yaphiach lo (H7896, H3468, H6315): I will set him in safety -- from the one who puffs at him (Psalm 10:5's snort), or, as many read it, 'the safety he pants for'. Either way the needy get the thing the arrogant claimed: security.

6.text: The LORD's words are pure words -- like silver refined in an earthen crucible, purified seven times over.
6.amp: The words [imrah] of the LORD [YHWH] are pure [tahor] words [imrah]: as silver [keseph] tried [tsaraph -- refined] in a furnace of earth [eretz], purified seven times [shibatayim].
6.notes: imrot YHWH amarot tehorot (H565, H3068, H2889): the LORD's sayings are PURE sayings -- set deliberately against the smooth, empty, double speech of verses 2-4; keseph tsaruph ba-alil la-aretz (H3701, H6884, H776): silver refined in a crucible of earth -- alil, found only here, is usually taken as a smelting crucible or furnace -- mezuqqaq shibatayim (H7659): purified seven times, the number of completeness. No slag, no second heart; what He says is exactly what is.

7.text: You, O LORD, will keep them; You will guard each one from this generation forever.
7.amp: You shall keep [shamar] them, O LORD [YHWH], You shall preserve [natsar -- guard] them ['him, that is, every one of them', natsar, the KJV margin] from this [zu] generation [dor] for ever [olam].
7.notes: attah-YHWH tishmerem (H3068, H8104): You will KEEP them -- the objects are the afflicted of verse 5, or the pure words of verse 6; the Hebrew allows both and the church has prayed both. titsrennu min-ha-dor zu le-olam (H5341, H1755, H2098, H5769): guard 'him', the margin's singular -- each one -- from this generation forever. A generation of smooth tongues is survivable if God is the keeper.

8.text: The wicked strut about on every side, when what is vile is exalted among the sons of men.
8.amp: The wicked [rasha] walk [halak] on every side, when the vilest men ['of the sons of the men', ben adam, the KJV margin] are exalted [rum].
8.notes: sabib reshaim yithallakhun (H7563, H1980): the wicked walk ABOUT -- the hithpael, strutting, patrolling -- on every side; ke-rum zullut li-bene adam (H7311, H1121, H120): when zullut, cheapness, vileness, is exalted among the sons of men. The psalm ends where it began, in a bad generation -- but between the two descriptions God has spoken (v. 5) and His words have been assayed (v. 6). The last word is realism, not despair.
